items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

The summer solstice has long been significant for Indigenous peoples on these lands as a time to honour the sun and celebrate the warmth, light, crops and plants it gives to us. More recently, all Canadians have been invited to celebrate the heritage, cultures and contributions of First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples on National Indigenous Peoples Day.

Residents of Waterloo are encouraged to explore learning resources at the Library, attend celebratory events and support local Indigenous artists, business owners and organizations. Through action, we can create a community where Indigenous knowledge is valued and respected, and where all Indigenous people belong and thrive.

items.title: Official Plan Review: Draft Official Plan
notes: Prepared By: Adam Lauder and Ric Martins
Ric Martins gave a presentation highlighting the intent and scope of the Official Plan Review. He then responded to questions of Council. Adam Lauder also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Housing Accelerator Fund - Corridor
notes: Tanja Curic offered some introductory remarks, outlining the staff report findings. She then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Property Tax Exemption for Affordable
notes: Sean Campbell, Executive Director, Union Co-operative gave a presentation speaking about the importance of the affordable housing property tax exemption to the community, and in favour of it.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-14,
notes: Tristin Deveau gave a presentation outlining the proposed zoning by-law amendment, including background on the station area planning process and the Official Plan Review.
He then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: Inclusionary Zoning Official Plan
notes: Michelle Lee gave a presentation providing a high-level overview of Inclusionary Zoning, including its benefits, the impact on the community, and the rules surrounding eligibility.
She then responded to questions of Council.
Reema Masri, Member, Waterloo Region Home Builders Association spoke about the need for an ongoing framework and highlight concerns on behalf of the association and responded to questions of Council.

Melissa Durrell, Spokesperson, Build Urban and Joseph Puopolo, Co-Chair, Build Urban spoke about the need for further dialogue and consultation. They asked for clarification on the different station types – prime, established, emerging – and how they were assigned. Joseph Puopolo responded to questions of Council. Michelle Lee responded to questions of Council.

Paul Leveck, President, Urban Legend Developments Ltd. gave a presentation discussing the potential outcomes of Inclusionary Zoning on the housing industry, and offered alternative solutions to the affordable housing situation.

Kristen Barisdale, GSP Group spoke in support of inclusionary zoning as a regulatory framework, but requested that Council defer the implementation of inclusionary zoning until the Official Plan Review is complete.
Ashwin Annamalai, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the need for more affordable housing in the City, and in support of Inclusionary Zoning, despite its limits.
Shiva Subramanian, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the precarious situations renters face, and the need for more affordable housing.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.
Michelle Lee responded to questions of Council. Adam Lauder also responded to questions of Council.

Councillors Bodaly and Vasic moved and seconded the main motion as recommended by staff. Councillor Freeman requested an additional recommendation which was voted on separately in advance of the main motion.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Hanmer gave a shout out to the Westvale Community Association who held their festival this past weekend. She offered thanks to the active transportation staff who were there with their booth. The event had many people in attendance and even set off their fireworks on time.

Councillor Vasic also joined some neighbourhood events this past weekend. Southwick Streets celebrated their 30th Neighbourhood BBQ and the Cardinal Crescent neighbourhood held a pot luck. Both events had musical performances.

Councillor Roe wanted to mention that the World Refugee Day community event was on Saturday, June 22. It was very well attended, and a great event. The Walk with Refugees for a Stronger Canada went from TheMuseum in Kitchener to the Multicultural Festival.

Mayor McCabe talked about the Special Council Meeting at the Region this morning, where the Executive Director of the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO) and their policy director did a presentation with some provincial and federal representatives.
It was an opportunity for senior staff from the Region and AMO to provide an overview of the challenges with the current funding programs for municipalities.

motions.text: 1. That IPPW2024-008 be approved. 2. That the City-initiated Official Plan Amendment 50 for the purposes of introducing Inclusionary Zoning within Protected Major Transit Station Areas be adopted, in the form shown in the Official Plan Amendment attached to Report IPPW2024-008 as Appendix ‘A’ and accordingly forwarded to the Region of Waterloo for approval. 3. That the City-initiated Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-15 to amend Zoning By-law 2018-050 be approved in the form shown in the “Proposed By-law Amendment” attached to Report IPPW2024-008 as Appendix ‘B’. 4. That staff be directed to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Region of Waterloo outlining roles and responsibilities in relation to administration of Inclusionary Zoning, to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning. 5. That staff be directed to monitor local market conditions and engage with the community and the development industry, as appropriate, and report back to Council no later than the end of 2024, 2026, 2028 and 2030, with recommendations on whether Inclusionary Zoning requirements should continue to be advanced or modified, within the Market Area categorizations, and as set out in Report IPPW2024-008.
motions.text_html:
1. That IPPW2024-008 be approved.

2. That the City-initiated Official Plan Amendment 50 for the purposes of introducing Inclusionary Zoning within Protected Major Transit Station Areas be adopted, in the form shown in the Official Plan Amendment attached to Report IPPW2024-008 as Appendix ‘A’ and accordingly forwarded to the Region of Waterloo for approval.

3. That the City-initiated Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-15 to amend Zoning By-law 2018-050 be approved in the form shown in the “Proposed By-law Amendment” attached to Report IPPW2024-008 as Appendix ‘B’.

4. That staff be directed to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Region of Waterloo outlining roles and responsibilities in relation to administration of Inclusionary Zoning, to the satisfaction of the Director of Planning.

5. That staff be directed to monitor local market conditions and engage with the community and the development industry, as appropriate, and report back to Council no later than the end of 2024, 2026, 2028 and 2030, with recommendations on whether Inclusionary Zoning requirements should continue to be advanced or modified, within the Market Area categorizations, and as set out in Report IPPW2024-008.
